description:
Discovery and proposed prerequisite for zaq-h2i.3. Approval status: pending human decision under docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md Phase 2 (uncovered architectural contract) and issue 3 explicit capability-gap gate. Do not change adapters/shared contracts before approval.

Evidence and ownership:
- Bridge (lib/zaq/channels/bridge.ex): optional capability_snapshot/1 callback and capability_snapshot/2 provider/config-scoped projection. normalize_capability_snapshot/2 retains only kind, required, resolved, unsupported, labels; extra metadata is discarded.
- Channels.Api (lib/zaq/channels/api.ex) already exposes :channel_capability_snapshot; it forwards provider plus scoped request. Reuse it, with config_id for selected connection and provider scope only for a new form.
- JidoChatBridge (lib/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge.ex) obtains delivery statuses from Jido.Chat.Capabilities.channel_capabilities/1 and Adapter.capabilities/1. Locked jido_chat 1.2.1 has no file_requirements or file_transfer_mode API or configurable limit definitions.
- Locked Mattermost 93025d5205e070eebbecf89e539d32bdf1fde3ff declares send_file native, post_message fallback and generic edit_message native, but no file_requirements/configurable_max_file_size declaration. Generic edit support does not establish attachment-edit support. Other transfer modes/limit facts must remain unresolved until declared by their adapter.
- EmailBridge (lib/zaq/channels/email_bridge.ex) reports text/threads native only; this remains true. Email attachment receiving is not delivery. SMTP configuration capability may exist independently of completed attachment sending.
- Reference old-worktree settings: channel max_file_size and send_on_file_failure; SMTP max_encoded_message_bytes and max_attachments_per_message, decimal MB inputs. Its later Jido dependency revisions do not establish capabilities of this branch. No reference tests read/copied.

Proposed smallest compatible extension for review:
1. Add optional Bridge file_delivery_capabilities/1 callback, collected by existing capability_snapshot/2 and exposed as optional top-level file_delivery metadata. Keep existing raw capability_snapshot/1 results, resolved support statuses, required/unsupported lists, labels and ingress mode meanings unchanged. No new endpoint. Missing callback means unavailable metadata; never infer limits or support by provider name.
2. file_delivery metadata describes transfer_mode (:upload_then_publish, :send_with_attachments, or unresolved), supports_attachment_edits (explicit fact, not inferred from edit_messages), and limits keyed by the five existing struct limit names: max_attachment_bytes, max_attachment_bytes_per_message, max_encoded_message_bytes, max_upload_request_bytes, max_attachments_per_message. Each limit definition contains value (positive integer, unresolved, or not_applicable), configurable boolean and required boolean. Configuration metadata alone never adds resolved.file support. SMTP can declare configurable required encoded-message/count settings and optional per-file override while retaining unsupported sending. Exact adapter transport facts require verified declarations, not shared-provider cases.
3. Jido metadata must come through an optional adapter-owned metadata declaration, or a separately approved dependency revision supplying that declaration; no edits in ignored deps and no copy of the old worktree implementation. Until declared, capability facts stay unavailable/unresolved. This prerequisite must establish that concrete source before generic consumer implementation.
4. Shared pure ConnectorConfig file-settings contract persists settings[file_delivery] containing only positive integer bytes/count overrides and send_on_file_failure boolean (default true). Existing branch has no old file keys to migrate. UI decimal MB uses 1000000 bytes; parse decimal strings exactly to whole bytes, at most six fractional decimal digits, reject fractional bytes/exponents/floats rather than round. Blank optional overrides remove the override and fall back to declared value; missing values remain unresolved. Fixed limits render read-only and cannot be raised/overridden; configurable values cannot exceed a known ceiling. Required unresolved configuration produces field errors.
5. One pure Channels.TransportRequirementsResolver.resolve(snapshot, selected_connection) returns {:ok, unchanged TransportRequirements struct} or explicit unsupported, capabilities_unavailable, missing/invalid configuration or unresolved-required-fact errors. Config controls failure_policy continue/abort; adapter facts cannot supply policy. Known transport ceilings win over any override. Unknown optional byte limits remain unresolved, explicit not_applicable remains distinct. Transfer mode and positive count are required for a successful struct. Thread support uses existing native/fallback support semantics; attachment-edit support needs its own fact. No persistence, acquisition, planning, sends or new Action/tool endpoint.
6. BO uses existing NodeRouter/Event snapshot and Engine persistence boundaries; shared pure ConnectorConfig functions handle both normalization and validation. BO must not directly call the Channels resolver. If effective preview becomes a concrete need, assess an existing operation extension before adding an endpoint.

Action reuse: extend existing Bridge snapshot projection/callback support; reuse :channel_capability_snapshot and exact config identity. Resolver and numeric/metadata normalization are local-only pure domain/shared configuration functions: no authorization, I/O, retries or runtime dependency selection, so Actions/tool exposure add no useful execution contract. Adapter metadata is a prerequisite, not a missing composable business Action. Preserve all existing test behavior; the optional callback design avoids changing two EmailBridgeTest exact raw snapshot assertions.

Tests before implementation: extend owning BridgeTest/ApiTest and EmailBridgeTest only by adding original cases for optional metadata, absence, support/configuration separation and existing normalization. Preserve existing Jido/Mattermost declarations and tests. New callback/dependency work requires confirming approved scope first. Tests must produce expected red failures before implementation. Docs: Channels service guide and focused Bridge callback types/docs; no parallel policy document.

comments.text: Additional discovered API prerequisite: selected disabled connections cannot use current config_id capability lookup because Bridge.fetch_scoped_capability_config/2 requires enabled:true. Propose an additive configuration-inspection scope on the existing :channel_capability_snapshot request, preserving default runtime lookup semantics and provider/kind/archive checks, or justify provider-scope static metadata where no selected-specific transport facts exist. Concrete consumer: editing a disabled selected BO/SMTP connection. No new endpoint or secret projection. Exact source and scope must be agreed with the metadata contract before implementation.

User instructed continue after the concrete contract proposal. Proceed with the additive metadata extension, shared configuration contract and pure resolver. Preserve current support statuses/raw snapshots, dependency pins, issue 1 and all existing test behavior. Locked adapters without the optional metadata callback remain unavailable/unresolved; no provider-specific inference or ignored dependency edits. Configuration validation may remain incomplete while file sending is unsupported, but required configuration is enforced for supported file delivery and by the resolver. This preserves existing SMTP saves while explicitly marking values required for future file delivery.

Original TDD red confirmed: new capability projection/configuration-scope tests fail on missing file_delivery metadata and disabled-scope lookup; normalization/resolver tests fail for undefined new modules/APIs. Result: 2 properties and 7 tests failed, with 3 checks passed and 126 excluded by the focused API describe selector. Log /tmp/zaq-h2i-3-red.log. Dependency compilation and isolated test database preparation succeeded. New component/SMTP/persistence tests are written and will receive their own red run before wiring implementation. Existing tests remain untouched.

title: [zaq-h2i.3] Approve and supply file capability metadata contract
